subject: Cloud Computing
title: Event Sourcing
description: A fast breakdown of Event Sourcing for builders.

hook.text: Your bank doesn't update your balance — it stores every transaction. Your balance is calculated from the history.

buildup.text: Event sourcing stores every state change as an immutable event. The current state is derived by replaying all events.

discovery.text: You get a complete audit trail for free. You can reconstruct the state at any point in time by replaying events.

twist.text: Event stores grow forever. Replaying millions of events gets slow, requiring snapshots and careful management.

climax.text: Event sourcing shines in financial systems, audit-heavy domains, and anywhere history matters as much as the present.

punchline.text: Don't overwrite state. Record what happened. Replay the truth.

quiz.question: What is a key benefit of event sourcing?
options: A complete audit trail that lets you reconstruct state at any point in time
It eliminates the need for any database storage
Events are automatically deleted after processing

details.summary: Event sourcing stores every state change as an immutable event rather than overwriting current state. The current state is derived by replaying events. This creates a complete audit trail and enables time-travel debugging.
details.whyItMatters: Event sourcing provides a perfect history of what happened and why. It is essential in domains like finance and compliance where audit trails are mandatory.
takeaways: State is derived by replaying a sequence of immutable events
Every change is recorded and can never be lost
Enables rebuilding state to any point in time

faq.question: How does event sourcing differ from traditional CRUD?
faq.answer: CRUD overwrites the current record on each update, losing history. Event sourcing appends a new event for each change, preserving the full history. Current state is computed by replaying all events from the beginning or from a snapshot.

faq.question: What are the challenges of event sourcing?
faq.answer: Event stores grow large over time, requiring snapshots for performance. Schema evolution of events is complex. Querying current state requires projections. The learning curve is steep for teams accustomed to traditional database patterns.
